As mentioned in the sidebar, administering P2P networks can be a challenge, and keeping spammers, flooding and vote brigading in check is a difficult problem.

Let's look at one of the most successful P2P systems out there, BitTorrent. This protocol performs most of its work via P2P, and while originally discovery relied on "tracker" servers, this function is now mostly performed via a distributed hash table - also P2P. Still, for an end user to be able to connect to a "torrent" containing the content he wants, he must still visit a conventional internet service - often a web server, though other methods exist - to obtain at the minimum the "infohash" for the data. While there have been extensions proposed for searching via the P2P network, these are potentially subject to attack by spammers or malware purveyors.

While making this system run entirely via P2P would result in the greatest resiliency in the face of government censorship and the lowest operating expenses, it would be exceedingly difficult to keep spam and brigading in check, as well as to keep denial-of-service attacks from happening.

I can think of a few ways to organize central service, some more resilient than others, and over time I'll post replies here regarding each. Note that, for flexibility's sake, more than one model might be implemented at the same time.
